elements.element: Customer owns each Deliverable created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 instead states that Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer, whether or not it is a Deliverable.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not grant Customer ownership of work product and addresses only Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in the Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: There is no assignment by Vendor; Section 14.2 expressly preserves Vendor's exclusive ownership of Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of all of its pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 says Vendor retains Vendor Technology, and the added language covers generic tools and know-how, but the supplied text does not establish that these terms encompass all Vendor pre-existing IP.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to any Vendor pre-existing IP embedded in a Deliverable.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 applies a licence to incorporated Vendor Technology, but the supplied text does not establish that all Vendor pre-existing IP embedded in a Deliverable falls within Vendor Technology or the referenced licence.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor pre-existing IP is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 expressly applies a perpetual licence to Vendor Technology incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor pre-existing IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The added language makes the Section 14.2 Deliverable licence irrevocable, but it does not state that the separate Section 13.2 licence applicable to embedded Vendor Technology is irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor pre-existing IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The added language makes the Section 14.2 Deliverable licence royalty-free, but the terms of the separate Section 13.2 licence applicable to embedded Vendor Technology are not supplied and are not expressly made royalty-free here.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no operative language addressing ownership of or rights in Customer Data.

elements.element: The ownership arrangement creates no joint ownership.
elements.evidence: Deliverables are expressly owned exclusively by Vendor, Vendor retains Vendor Technology, and Customer receives licence rights rather than co-ownership rights.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The added operative language expressly states that Vendor owns its generic tools.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: The added operative language expressly states that Vendor owns its know-how.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to each Deliverable.
elements.evidence: The added language states that Customer receives a licence to each Deliverable.

elements.element: The Deliverable licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly describes the licence as perpetual.

elements.element: The Deliverable licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly describes the licence as irrevocable and negates Section 14.2's revocability.

elements.element: The Deliverable licence is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly describes the licence as worldwide.

elements.element: The Deliverable licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly describes the licence as royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may use each Deliverable.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly grants Customer the right to use each Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer may modify each Deliverable.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly grants Customer the right to modify each Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense each Deliverable.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly grants Customer the right to sublicense each Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer may exercise the licensed rights for its business.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits the licensed rights to be exercised for Customer's business.

result.reason: The rendered clause fully reaches the fallback: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how, while Customer receives the required perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free rights to use, modify, and sublicense Deliverables for its business. It does not reach the preferred position because Vendor retains exclusive Deliverable ownership, no assignment or Customer work-product ownership is provided, Customer Data is omitted, and the required embedded-IP scope and licence terms are incomplete. It is not minimal because negating “non-transferable” appears to make the licence transferable, an additional right beyond the fallback's required sublicensing right. Although the express override preserves the intended fallback and leaves unrelated provisions effective, the append-only drafting retains directly contrary language in Section 14.2 and uses an awkward, potentially ambiguous double negative.
